title: Security needs cartography and decision lattice for enterprise request triage
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Enterprise customers submit a wide range of security and compliance asks (SOC2 evidence, ISO questionnaires, HIPAA scoping, GDPR/DPA clauses, vendor security questionnaires). Current intake is inconsistent: PMs and SEs manually interpret asks, leading to variable SLAs, duplicated effort, and missed contractual timelines. Goal: build a deterministic triage framework that maps inbound asks to an actionable priority and routing lane using a reusable ‘cartography’ of controls, risk signals, and implementation effort estimates.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A documented cartography matrix that maps common ask types (SOC2 control request, ISO evidence, DPA clause, HIPAA data flow question, vendor questionnaire) to a canonical set of signals (regulatory scope, deal ARR band, data residency risk, SLA request, technical effort).
2) A decision lattice (scoring rules) that produces a priority label (P0/P1/P2) and a recommended lane (self-serve, concierge, legal-review, engineering-scope) for 90% of incoming requests in a sample of 200 recent tickets.
3) Automation prototype that tags new intake with the derived signals and priority in the intake queue.
4) Playbook pages and owner assignments for each lane with expected SLA windows and required artifacts.
5) Stakeholder sign-off from Security, Legal, and Sales Engineering on the mapping and SLAs.
proposed_workflow: 1) Inbound ask lands in Intake form (structured + free text). 2) NLP classifier extracts ask type and initial signals (customer region, sensitive data, contract stage). 3) Decision lattice applies weighted rules to compute priority and lane. 4) If 'concierge' or 'engineering' lane, auto-create child ticket routed to respective queue; if 'legal-review', attach standard evidence template and notify Legal. 5) Feedback loop: when an item is closed, update the cartography scoring weights based on actual elapsed effort and outcome. Automation will live in Intake -> triage lambda -> Linear auto-labeling.
success_metrics:
- Reduce median time-to-first-response for high-impact security asks from 4 business days to 1 business day.
- Increase percentage of requests auto-classified to a lane from ~30% to >=80%.
- Reduce engineering rework on triaged asks by 25% (measured by reopened tickets and extra-scope tags).
- SLA adherence: 95% of P0/P1 items acknowledged within target windows after rollout.
risks:
- Overfitting the lattice to historical tickets may encode past mistakes.
- False negatives on high-risk asks (missing a HIPAA-scoped request) leading to contractual exposure.
- Classifier performance degrades for noisy free-text submissions.
- Cross-team coordination (Legal/Security/SE) could delay playbook approval.
open_questions:
- What minimum structured fields do Sales/Support need to collect to reliably calculate signals?
- Should priority weigh deal stage (legal hold) more heavily than technical complexity?
- Is there appetite to expose an SLA promise in the public-facing portal or keep SLAs internal?
- Which events should trigger automatic escalation to Security (e.g., mentions of PHI, PCI scopes, or data residency requests)?
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (2 sprints): build cartography matrix and manual rule-based lattice; instrument Intake form changes. Phase 2 (3 sprints): build lightweight classifier (text -> ask-type), integrate with Linear APIs for auto-labeling, add basic telemetry. Phase 3 (ongoing): refine weights with closed-loop telemetry, shift rules to ML model if rule maintenance cost grows. Keep Legal as gate for any automation that affects contract language. Retain human-in-loop for any new ask type for first 30 days.
